Thanks for the recap - that matches our notes. A few answers from our side to help you prioritize the questionnaire:

1) SOC 2: We strongly prefer a current SOC 2 Type II report. If you are in-progress, an attestation + expected completion date can be considered, but that will trigger an internal risk review and may require compensating controls.

3) SIEM: Preferred is live or near-real-time forward to Splunk. If not available, secure exports (S3/CSV) on a schedule are acceptable as a fallback.

Marissa / team / Jenna -

Thanks for the context. Below are concise answers you can paste into the questionnaire; happy to join the 7/22 call for any follow-ups.

SOC 2 status:
- Redwood Inference is SOC 2 Type II certified as of Nov 2025. We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA (we usually share through our secure compliance portal or an S3 link once NDA is complete).

Audit logging (admin activity and API logs):
- Admin activity logs: Records of console/API admin actions (user create/delete, role changes, policy updates, config changes). Each entry includes timestamp (UTC), actor (user/service account), action, target resource, IP address, and a change diff where applicable.
- API request logs: Per-request records containing timestamp, request id, authenticated principal, endpoint, request metadata (method, path, headers), response status, and tokenized metrics (latency, token counts). We do NOT log full prompt contents for hosted customers unless explicitly configured (we provide options for customer-managed logging depending on deployment).
- Retention: Default retention in hosted mode is 365 days. For Dedicated and Private deployments customers can configure retention policies. We provide secure export to customer-managed S3 for longer-term archival (e.g., 7 years) and can assist with lifecycle policies.
- Export formats & transport: Exports are available as newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) or compressed CSV. For hosted customers we support encrypted S3 exports to a customer bucket (server-side encryption with SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS). For Dedicated/Private, we support direct streaming to the customer's SIEM (Syslog over TLS, Splunk HEC) or secure log-forwarders.
- Immutability & integrity: For Private deployments we support hardware-backed WORM (write-once) configurations on customer-managed storage. For hosted exports we provide append-only logs with signed checksums and tamper-evident headers; we can generate periodic Merkle-tree based integrity manifests on request for compliance reviews.
- Access controls & auditing: Log access is restricted to authorized roles; we maintain access audit trails and can provide per-request access logs for the exported archives.

GDPR / HIPAA notes:
- GDPR: We provide a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and region-based data residency options. Customers control export/retention and can request deletion of customer-controlled data.
- HIPAA: Redwood supports HIPAA compliance for covered workloads (BAA available). We encrypt data at rest and in transit and support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Private/Dedicated deployments.

Other notes / limitations to call out:
- Hosted: Default retention 1 year, exports available; immutability guarantees for exported archives depend on customer-managed storage configuration.
- Dedicated: Greater flexibility for retention and SIEM integration; can set longer on-instance retention windows.
- Private/on-prem: Full control - WORM and immutable storage options available subject to customer infra.

2) Rishi and I can join the 7/22 9:30 AM PST technical sync - can you confirm and send a calendar invite, Jenna?
